newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU threatens court action in Spain TV decoder row.
newsitem.headline: EU threatens court action in Spain TV decoder row.

text.p: The European Commission threatened on Wednesday to take Spain to court over a law on decoders for digital pay-TV services that it says restricts free trade.

The Commission -- intervening in a dispute between the government, the opposition Socialist Party and their supporting media groups -- gave Madrid one month to amend the law or face possible action before the European Court of Justice.
The Spanish law requires digital TV operators to provide compatible decoders to ensure that consumers can receive a variety of programmes using one piece of equipment.

But it says that in the absence of an agreement between companies, the multicrypt system must be adopted -- prompting a complaint from TV operator Canal Plus, whose decoders are based on the competing "simulcrypt" technology.

The Commission, arguing that the law violates EU treaty provisions on free movement of goods and services, sent Spain a "letter of formal notice" last month and asked the government to respond within 15 days.
The new action, known as a "reasoned opinion", is the second stage of proceedings that can lead to action before the EU court.
Canal Plus has teamed up with Spanish media group Prisa, which controls influential left-wing newspaper El Pais, to launch the Canalsatelite digital TV operation in Spain.
Telecommunications operator Telefonica de Espana and state television RTVE are planning to launch a rival package, Via Digital, in September using the mulitcrypt system.
Among other complaints, the Commission said Spain had violated EU law by failing to notify it before adopting the decoder rules.
